task_data.prompt: The figure shows a task-dependency directed acyclic graph (DAG) representing a parallel computation pipeline. Tasks are nodes $S, A, B, C, D, E, F, T$, where $S$ is entry and $T$ is terminal. Directed edges $(u, v)$ represent precedence with latency in milliseconds ($\text{ms}$). Assuming tasks start immediately once all predecessors complete, determine the critical path duration (maximum latency from $S$ to $T$). Answer in ms as a 2 significant figure number without units. Intermediate calculations to 6 significant figures. Unstated constants to 4 significant figures.
task_data.image_description: Directed acyclic graph with entry S, terminal T. 8 nodes, 15 directed edges with latency labels (ms). Crossing edges: (S,C) crosses (A,D); (B,E) crosses (A,D); (C,F) crosses (D,E); (D,T) crosses (E,F).
task_data.solution:
Step 1: Identify all 8 nodes and directed edge latencies (ms).
Step 2: Trace candidate directed paths from source $S$ to $T$.
Step 3: Evaluate path $S \to A \to D$: latency is $14+22=36\text{ ms}$.
Step 4: Continue along $S \to A \to D \to E \to F \to T$: critical path is $76\text{ ms}$.
Step 5: Ground Truth Final Answer is 76.
task_data.failure_justification: Both models failed to trace the directed topological critical path of the graph. The crossing edges caused models to misread connections or overlook the optimal sub-path detour $D \to E \to F$ ($12+8=20\text{ ms}$) in favor of $D \to F$ ($19\text{ ms}$) or $D \to T$ ($28\text{ ms}$).
